memory_update.text: LOPE is the cleanest US-listed direct supplier candidate for online program enablement and university outsourcing because revenue is explicitly tied to services agreements with university partners.
COUR should be tracked as a platform/distribution model for university online degrees and credentials, not as a traditional full-service OPM.
STRA offers a second-order path into online degree demand through employer education-benefit administration and transferable online general-education credits.

Many historically important OPM assets are private, sold, merged, or delisted; later layers should map private reference competitors such as Risepoint/Academic Partnerships and former OPM assets at Pearson/Wiley to benchmark public candidates.

node: Online program enablement and university outsourcing
summary: Layer 1B expansion for online program enablement finds a narrow US-listed universe. The most direct public exposure is Grand Canyon Education, which discloses university-services agreements providing integrated technology, academic, marketing, communications, and back-office services for tuition/fee revenue share. Coursera is a platform-style university distribution and online-degree partner rather than a labor-heavy OPM. Strategic Education is a hybrid operator plus second-order employer/university benefits infrastructure through Workforce Edge and Sophia. Perdoceo is included only as a reference/operator comp because it owns accredited institutions rather than supplying outside universities. The underfollowed chokepoint to test is not generic online learning demand, but whether student acquisition, retention support, compliance workflows, credit-transfer infrastructure, and long-duration institutional relationships are scarce enough to earn durable economics.
